tracks.title: Requiem in C minor: Introitus et Kyrie
tracks.fact: Beethoven considered Cherubini the greatest living composer of his time, and this Requiem was performed at Beethoven's funeral in 1827.
tracks.source_verification: Deane, Basil. 'Luigi Cherubini: His Life and Work', Oxford University Press, 1965, p. 42.

tracks.title: Médée (Medea): Overture
tracks.fact: Brahms admired the overture to Medea immensely, keeping it as a permanent reference score in his study.
tracks.source_verification: Paris Opera Archives, Historical Record of Médée (1797).

tracks.title: Symphony in D major: I. Largo - Allegro molto
tracks.fact: Cherubini's only symphony was commissioned directly by the Royal Philharmonic Society in London in 1815.
tracks.source_verification: Royal Philharmonic Society Archive, London Records (1815).

tracks.title: Marche funèbre
tracks.fact: Composed in 1820 following the assassination of the Duke of Berry, noted for its unusually stark instrumentation.

tracks.title: String Quartet No. 1 in E-flat major
tracks.fact: Cherubini began writing string quartets only after turning fifty, directly modeling them on Haydn's late works.
tracks.source_verification: Cobbett's Cyclopedic Survey of Chamber Music, Vol. 1.

tracks.title: Ave Maria
tracks.fact: An intimate sacred piece written for soprano and English horn during his service at the Royal Chapel in Paris.

event_note: New Year's Eve Special: Celebrating the tradition of festive symphonic gala concerts and Strauss waltzes

tracks.title: The Blue Danube, Op. 314
tracks.fact: Originally written as a choral piece with somewhat cynical lyrics about politics, it quickly became the unofficial national anthem of Austria.
tracks.source_verification: Kamp, Sicherheit. 'Johann Strauss: King of Waltz', Vienna, 1931.

tracks.title: Die Fledermaus: Overture
tracks.fact: Strauss composed the entire overture to his master operetta in just 42 hours during a frantic weekend in Vienna.

tracks.title: Tales from the Vienna Woods, Op. 325
tracks.fact: Strauss included a rare folk instrument called a zither in the introduction to capture authentic Austrian rustic atmosphere.
tracks.source_verification: Vienna Philharmonic New Year's Concert Documentation.

tracks.title: Emperor Waltz, Op. 437
tracks.fact: Written to commemorate the 40th anniversary of Emperor Franz Joseph I's accession to the Austro-Hungarian throne.
tracks.source_verification: Austrian National Library Music Collection, MS 44821.

tracks.title: Tritsch-Tratsch-Polka, Op. 214
tracks.fact: The title refers to Vienna's notorious obsession with neighborhood gossip and chitchat, mirrored in the frantic, sparkling violin lines.
tracks.source_verification: Sachs, Curt. 'World History of the Dance', New York, 1937.

tracks.title: Radetzky March, Op. 228 (arranged)
tracks.fact: Composed by Johann Strauss I to honor Field Marshal Radetzky, it serves as the traditional thunderous closing encore of the Vienna New Year's Concert.
